<result>## Review: `fix/230-defer-offscreen-listing-images`

Branch carries no commits (`git log main..HEAD` is empty); everything is in the working tree. Reviewed all of it, plus the surrounding code the change leans on.

---

## Findings

### 1. The decode assertion waits a fixed 3s that the file's own measurements say is too short — **defect** (confidence 80)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/e2e/image-deferral.spec.ts:95`

```ts
await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight))
await page.waitForTimeout(3000)
```

The `requested.size > initial` assertion only needs requests *issued*, and 3s is ample for that. The `broken === 0` check at line 114 needs them **decoded**, and the same file records (line 68) that "the slowest optimisation measured on a constrained server was 3253ms" with a median of 2343ms on two cores — and explicitly notes that a request "is issued long before it completes". The second wait reuses a number that was justified for the weaker property.

Concrete failure: CI runs a fresh composed stack, so `.next/cache/images` is cold. `image-deferral.spec.ts` sorts before `image-delivery.spec.ts`, so nothing has warmed the below-fold variants. Scrolling to the bottom of a 5038px document brings the remaining deferred cards inside the 1200px margin at once — I measured 9 optimiser requests before scrolling and 20 after, so ~11 `sharp` jobs queue on two shared cores. The last row's three on-screen images are somewhere in that queue; at a 2343ms median they routinely will not have `naturalWidth > 0` at 3000ms. `playwright.config.ts` sets `retries: 0`, so that is a hard red on a page that is behaving correctly — the same class of CI failure #230 exists to remove.

Fix: keep the 3s wait for the request-count assertion, and poll the decode predicate instead of timing it. `await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(...), { timeout: 15_000 }).toBe(0)` fits inside the 30s test budget (3s + 3s + 15s) and fails with the same message when deferral genuinely breaks.

---

### 2. The component doc comment asserts a contract that no guard holds, and names the wrong sibling surface — **refinement** (confidence 85)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/src/components/listing-image.tsx:57` and `:61-66`

Two claims in the doc block do not hold:

**a. The squareness contract.** Line 61: *"`aspect-square` is a claim about the catalogue, not a guess: every source under `public/images` is 1024x1024, held there by `config/catalogue_images.json` and `tests/scripts/test_image_encoding.py`."* Neither file holds that. `catalogue_images.json` carries `maxDimension` only, and `test_image_encoding.py:196` and `:220` both test `if max(width, height) > MAX_DIMENSION` — a long-edge ceiling. A 1024x600 WebP passes every guard in the repository.

This matters because the change *introduces* the dependency. The old markup was `width={350} height={350}` plus `h-auto`, which took its box from the source's own ratio; the new wrapper hard-codes `aspect-square` and the image is `w-full h-auto`, so a non-square source letterboxes with a `bg-zinc-200` strip under it and nothing turns red. Measured the current state: all 853 catalogue WebPs are 1024x1024 (the single 1024x450 is the hero background, which is on the full-bleed allowlist and never reaches this component), so nothing renders wrong today. The comment is what a future maintainer would rely on when adding an image.

Fix: either state it as an observation ("every source is 1024x1024 today; nothing enforces the ratio") or add the assertion to `test_image_encoding.py`, which already reads both dimensions and would need `width == height`.

**b. The tone precedent.** Line 57: *"It is the same tone the category grid already uses."* The category grid at `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/src/app/products/category/[slug]/page.tsx:47` uses `bg-gray-200`, not `bg-zinc-200`. The `bg-zinc-200` precedent is `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/src/app/about/page.tsx:29`. The contrast ratios quoted just above it are yours and measured; only the attribution is wrong.

---

### 3. `ROOT_MARGIN` is the tuning knob nothing measures — **refinement** (confidence 78)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/src/components/listing-image.tsx:104`, `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/src/components/listing-image.test.tsx:32`

The unit test's fake observer takes only the callback:

```ts
constructor(callback: IntersectionObserverCallback) {
  callbacks.push(callback)
}
```

The options argument is discarded, so nothing anywhere observes that `{ rootMargin: ROOT_MARGIN }` is passed at all. Delete that second argument — or set it to `0px` — and every unit test still passes, and `image-deferral.spec.ts` gets *better*: fewer initial requests, comfortably under the bound. The user-visible result is the pop-in the 1200px value was measured against (your own note: at 1000ms optimiser latency, 14 of 20 cards grey as they enter). The one regression the constant exists to prevent is the one direction no guard can see, in a file whose sibling comment says the knobs are "tuned against pop-in rather than against this bound".

Fix: capture the second constructor argument in the stub and assert `rootMargin` is `'1200px'` on the deferred-render test. One line each, and it makes the constant's value a fact rather than a comment.

---

## Your four questions

**`eager={i <= 1}`** — acceptable as written. Expressing it as a card count means threading a cumulative index across categories (`categories.slice(0, i).reduce(...)`), which is more machinery producing the same unguarded number, and the real invariant genuinely is per-category: the grid restarts at each `Block` with an `h2` and a description between, so "the first two categories" is the unit the layout actually has. What is worth knowing is that nothing fails if it becomes wrong in the *shrinking* direction — a taller hero or a fourth product per category leaves above-fold cards deferred again, and `MAX_INITIAL_REQUESTS` is an upper bound only. Not a finding; the comment already states the measurement.

**`bg-zinc-200` contrast** — the reasoning is sound, not self-serving. 1.4.11 scopes to UI components and graphical objects required to understand the content; this is the transient loading state of an `alt=""` image whose card takes its accessible name entirely from the link text, so neither clause reaches it. The case where the argument stops holding is the permanent one, which is exactly what #261 is. Only the attribution in the comment is wrong (finding 2b).

**Can the polyfill produce vacuous passes?** Bounded today, and I agree with `verifier`. `ListingImage` is the only `IntersectionObserver` consumer in `src/` (grepped), and `listing-image.test.tsx` stubs its own via `vi.stubGlobal`, so it never touches the polyfill. The one place the polyfill actually applies is `src/app/page.test.tsx`, which renders `await Home()` and therefore renders 14 of the 20 cards as empty boxes. Its single assertion targets `catalogue[0].products[0]`, which is eager, so it is not vacuous now. The exposure is a *future* jsdom assertion phrased over "every card's image", which would silently measure 6 of 20. That is worth one sentence in the setup comment; it is not a defect in this change.

It only measures at 1440x900, where I re-measured 9 against your 9, so there are 3 of headroom, and the regressions it must catch all land at 20 (lazy-only, observer dropped, `eager` widened to every category). input.command:
gh issue create --title "Two surfaces depend on catalogue images being square, and nothing enforces it" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Found by `code-review` while reviewing the fix for #230.

## What is unheld

`config/catalogue_images.json` and `tests/scripts/test_image_encoding.py` bound the **long edge** only. The guard reads:

```python
if max(width, height) > MAX_DIMENSION:
```

So a 1024x600 WebP satisfies every check in the repository. Nothing anywhere asserts `width == height`.

## Two rendering surfaces assume otherwise

Both put the image in a fixed-ratio box, and they fail differently:

- `apps/web/src/app/products/category/[slug]/page.tsx:47` — `aspect-square ... overflow-hidden` with the image `object-cover`. A non-square source is **cropped**, silently and plausibly, so the product's shape is wrong and nothing looks broken.
- `apps/web/src/components/listing-image.tsx` (new, from #230) — `aspect-square` on the wrapper with the image `w-full h-auto`. A non-square source is **letterboxed**, leaving a strip of `bg-zinc-200` under it.

The second one is newly introduced. The markup it replaces used `width={350} height={350}` with `h-auto`, which took its box from the source's own ratio, so it degraded gracefully. That is worth being explicit about: #230's fix traded a graceful degradation for a reserved box, and the reserved box is what makes its zero-layout-shift result true.

## Measured

All 853 files under `apps/web/public/images` referenced by the catalogue are 1024x1024 today. The one exception, 1024x450, is `hero.png`'s successor, which is on the `fullBleed` allowlist in `config/catalogue_images.json` and never reaches either surface.

So nothing renders wrong right now. The gap is that the next image someone adds has no check standing between a non-square source and a silently cropped product card.

## Suggested fix

`test_image_encoding.py` already reads both dimensions for its `maxDimension` check, so the assertion is close to free — a `width == height` check over the same corpus, with the `fullBleed` entries exempt as they already are for the other rules.

Worth deciding at the same time whether squareness belongs in `config/catalogue_images.json` as a named part of the contract, next to `quality` and `maxDimension`, rather than living only in a test. That file is described in its own `_comment` as the shared contract between the converter and the guard, and the converter does not enforce a ratio either.

## Related

- #230 -- the change that made the second surface depend on this.
- #261 -- the other known limit of that change.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

Found by `code-review` while reviewing the fix for #230, which deliberately scoped itself to the home page.

## The same mechanism, on a bigger grid

`apps/web/src/app/products/category/[slug]/page.tsx:41-105` renders every product in a category with `priority={i < 3}` and everything else on `next/image`'s default lazy loading.

That is exactly the arrangement #230 measured on the home page: `loading="lazy"` is not a viewport test, and Chrome's threshold measured **~3900px**, so it speculatively fetches roughly four viewports ahead. `e2e/browse.spec.ts:153` records that a category runs **18 to 47 cards**, against the home page's 20 — so at 1440 a category landing sits comfortably inside that threshold and fires on the order of 21 concurrent optimiser jobs on a cold cache.

Each is a separate `sharp` decode-and-resize of a 1024px source. #230 measured those at a **2343ms median on two cores**, with an unrelated navigation issued during them going from 78ms to 500ms — and in CI, aborting outright.

## Why it was not fixed with #230

#230's fix is scoped to the home grid, and deliberately: it is one reviewable slice with a measurable before and after, and the home page is the surface whose contention was actually reproduced (it failed `browse.spec.ts` on #251).

Two things kept the category page out of that slice:

1. It needs a database to render, so it cannot be measured against a standalone `next start` the way the home page can. Every measurement behind #230 was taken without one.
2. `priority={i < 3}` is a real design decision on that page that the home grid does not have, and #180 is already open about how that cutoff interacts with the tablet breakpoint. Changing the loading strategy underneath an open question about the same three cards would tangle the two.

## What is now inconsistent

`apps/web/e2e/image-deferral.spec.ts` opens with "The listing pages request images for cards the visitor can reach, not for every card on the page" — plural — and then guards only `/`. That scope gap is deliberate but currently invisible; this issue is what makes it deliberate rather than an omission.

## Suggested direction

`ListingImage` from #230 is written to be reused: it takes `src`, `alt`, `sizes` and `eager`, and owns its own box. The category card already wraps its image in an `aspect-square ... overflow-hidden rounded-3xl bg-gray-200` div, which is the same shape the component now provides, so adopting it is mostly deletion.

Worth settling alongside:

- How `eager` should relate to the existing `priority={i < 3}`, and whether #180's row-split question is answered by the same change.
- That the category card's image is `object-cover` rather than `h-auto`, so the component would need to carry that difference or the two call sites would diverge -- see #262 for why the ratio matters here.
- Extending `image-deferral.spec.ts` to a category surface, which needs the composed stack rather than a bare server.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

All three findings addressed. Fresh round, please.

## Finding 1 (defect) — fixed

`e2e/image-deferral.spec.ts` now polls the decode predicate instead of timing it:

```ts
await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(...), {
  timeout: 15_000,
  message: 'on-screen cards whose image did not decode',
}).toBe(0)
```

The 3s wait is kept for the request-count assertion, which only needs requests issued. The comment records why the two differ and that 3s + 3s + 15s stays inside the 30s budget. Your reasoning was right and I had reused a number justified for the weaker property.

## Finding 2 (refinement) — both claims fixed

**2a.** The squareness paragraph now says it is an observation that nothing holds, names the long-edge-only shape of the guard (`max(width, height) > MAX_DIMENSION`), says a 1024x600 would letterbox with nothing turning red, and states that this component is where the dependency starts because the markup it replaces took its box from the source ratio. Filed as **#262**, which also covers the category grid's `object-cover` crop — you were right that the guard gap is pre-existing but that my change is what made a second surface depend on it.

**2b.** Attribution corrected: the about page's image band is the `bg-zinc-200` precedent; the category grid's is `bg-gray-200`, noted as a shade off.

## Finding 3 (refinement) — fixed and demonstrated

The unit stub now captures the constructor's second argument, and the deferred-render test asserts `options[0]?.rootMargin === '1200px'`. Demonstrated: deleting `{ rootMargin: ROOT_MARGIN }` from the component now fails that test, where before it passed everything. The comment records why this is the direction no other check can see — fewer requests is what both a correct margin and a deleted one look like to the journey.

## Also filed, from your "outside this change" section

**#263** — the category grid firing ~21 concurrent optimisations. I have left it out of this slice deliberately, and `image-deferral.spec.ts`'s header now says so and why: the page needs a database so none of my measurements could reach it, and `priority={i < 3}` is tangled with #180. That makes the plural in the header honest rather than aspirational.

## Verification since your review

- `HUSKY=0 make -C apps/web ci` — exit 0 (lint, both typechecks, unit tests, production build).
- `e2e/image-deferral.spec.ts` + `e2e/browse.spec.ts` against the composed stack — 7/7 pass.
- Mutation demo on the new assertion, as above.
- `next-env.d.ts` churn reverted again (#260).

## What I want from you

A fresh defect/refinement pass on the changed files. In particular:

- Is `expect.poll` at 15s the right shape, or does it now mask a genuine deferral failure by waiting long enough for anything to eventually load? I want to be sure I have not turned a sharp assertion into a soft one while fixing a flake.
- The `rootMargin` assertion pins a literal `'1200px'` in the test while the component holds it in `ROOT_MARGIN`. That is duplication by design — the test should fail if the constant changes without someone thinking about it — but tell me if you would rather it imported the constant.
- Anything in the two new issues' framing that misstates the code.

The stack is still up at http://localhost:3000, identity confirmed. Do not tear it down.

<result>## Re-review: fresh round

All three prior findings are fixed and the fixes are correct. `next-env.d.ts` is clean, `page.tsx` and `setup.ts` are unchanged from the last round. Two new refinements, no defects.

## Findings

### 1. The #263 deferral justification misstates why the category grid is out of scope — **refinement** (confidence 85)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/e2e/image-deferral.spec.ts:31-32`

> *"It is left out here rather than overlooked: it needs a database to render, so it cannot be measured the way every number above was."*

The first half is true — `getProductsByCategory` at `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/src/lib/products.ts:6` is a `prisma.category.findUnique`. The inference is not. These journeys run against the composed stack, which *has* the seeded database, and the category grid is already measured on it by two files in this directory: `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/e2e/image-delivery.spec.ts:101-108` resolves the slug from `/categories.json` and measures that surface across 21 widths at two densities, and `browse.spec.ts:172` navigates to `/products/category/tents` directly.

I measured it against your running stack with the same method as the header's home-page numbers, at 1440x900:

```
status 200
category cards: 21
optimiser requests before scrolling: 21
doc height: 3965
```

Twenty-one of twenty-one, on a document short enough that Chrome's ~3900px threshold swallows the whole page — the identical shape of finding to the home page's 18 of 20, obtained the same way. So the sentence claims an obstacle that does not exist, and it is the sentence a future reader will use to decide whether #263 is cheap.

The two honest reasons are already in the same paragraph and are sufficient on their own: the slice boundary, and the `priority={i < 3}` cutoff being an open question in #180. Fix: drop the database clause, or replace it with the measurement above — which would also give #263 a starting number it does not currently have.

---

### 2. The 30s budget arithmetic omits `page.goto`, which is the largest term on a cold cache — **refinement** (confidence 78)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/e2e/image-deferral.spec.ts:120`

> *"15s keeps the whole journey inside the 30s budget."*

The budget is 3s + 3s + 15s **+ `page.goto('/')`**. `goto` defaults to `waitUntil: 'load'`, and the `load` event waits on the six server-rendered images plus the three the observer inserts during hydration — nine optimisations, which is exactly what I measure on your stack.

That term is near zero warm and large cold. Measured just now on this 24-core machine, nine concurrent cold optimisations: 815ms wall, 527-800ms each. Scaled to the runner this change is about, #230's own body is the better number — *"still-pending after 21s: 20 x /\_next/image"*, i.e. roughly one image per second at two cores, so ~9s for `goto` to return. Add 3 + 3 and a poll that in the passing case still has to wait out the last row's share of eleven queued optimisations, and the test sits around 25s with about 5s of headroom. When it goes over, the failure is `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded`, which says less than the assertion it replaced.

The full-suite CI path is safe, but only by accident: `browse.spec.ts` sorts before `image-deferral.spec.ts` under `workers: 1`, and its first test scrolls the entire home page. The home card box is 350px at both 1280 (browse's default viewport) and 1440, so it warms the exact `w=384` variants this spec needs. Nothing states that dependency, and it breaks on a rename. The exposed path is the one AGENTS.md step 4 prescribes — `npx playwright test e2e/image-deferral.spec.ts` against a freshly composed stack.

Fix: `test.setTimeout(60_000)` on the scrolling test, with the cold-cache reason. There is precedent three files over — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso/apps/web/e2e/image-delivery.spec.ts:180` raises its own for the same reason and explains it. Then correct the comment to name `goto` as the term that dominates.

---

## Your three questions

**Is `expect.poll` at 15s now soft?** No. Waiting longer cannot turn a wrong result into a right one here — the predicate is `naturalWidth === 0`, and an image that 404s or never decodes stays at 0 forever, so a broken deferral still fails, just 12s later. What a fixed 3s bought that the poll does not is an implicit latency ceiling, and this file explicitly disclaims that property in its own header (*"the defect is the count, not the cost per image"*), so nothing that was being asserted stopped being asserted. The shape is right.

One thing worth knowing rather than acting on: the predicate returns 0 both when everything decoded and when there is nothing on screen to measure, so if the `PRODUCT_CARD img` selector ever stops matching — the image moving outside the `<a>`, say — the assertion passes on zero samples. That was equally true of the fixed wait, so the fix did not introduce it, and the `requested.size > initial` assertion above catches the failure mode that actually produces it (deferral that never resolves). I score it below the reporting bar and am not filing it; if you want the file's third vacuity guard for symmetry with the other two, polling the on-screen image count to be `> 0` is the one-liner.

**Literal `'1200px'` versus importing `ROOT_MARGIN`.** Keep the literal. Importing it would make the assertion tautological in the direction that matters: `expect(options[0]?.rootMargin).toBe(ROOT_MARGIN)` passes for `'0px'`, for `'50px'`, for any value someone edits the constant to — it would catch only the dropped-argument mutation, not the retuned-margin one, and the retuned one is the whole reason the assertion exists. That is the "measure what was produced, not what was asked for" rule in root `AGENTS.md`, and an imported constant measures the request. It would also mean exporting a constant purely for a test. I checked the failure path: with the options argument dropped, `options[0]` is `undefined`, `undefined?.rootMargin` is `undefined`, and `toBe('1200px')` fails rather than short-circuiting — so the optional chaining does not soften it. Your demonstration matches.

**Do the issue framings misstate the code?** #262's does not — I re-verified every claim in it. `test_image_encoding.py:196` and `:220` are both `max(width, height) > MAX_DIMENSION`, so a 1024x600 does pass everything. The count is exact: 853 catalogue WebPs at 1024x1024, with the 1024x450 hero being the full-bleed allowlist entry and outside `catalogue_images()`. "The markup it replaces took its box from the source's own ratio" is right for the loaded state — `width`/`height` give the UA an `aspect-ratio: auto 350 / 350`, whose `auto` keyword defers to the natural ratio once loaded, and `h-auto` lets it through. The category grid's `object-cover` crop at `products/category/[slug]/page.tsx:104` is stated correctly. 2b is correct in both directions: `about/page.tsx:29` is `bg-zinc-200`, `products/category/[slug]/page.tsx:47` is `bg-gray-200`. #263's framing is finding 1 above.

gh pr create --title "fix(web): fetch listing images for cards the visitor can reach" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes #230.

## What was wrong

The home page asked the optimiser for **18 images on first paint** while about three were on screen.

Every one of the twenty was already `loading="lazy"`. The markup was never wrong — `loading="lazy"` is a hint about a threshold the browser picks, not a viewport test, and Chrome's threshold measured **~3900px** here. At 1440x900 that reaches **4.3 viewports** down a 5038px document, so the browser fetched almost the entire page.

Each is a separate `sharp` decode-and-resize of a 1024px source:

| | before |
|---|---|
| Optimiser requests, 1440x900 | 18 of 20 |
| Optimiser requests, 390x844 | 9 |
| Per-image cost, 2-core server | 674ms min, **2343ms median**, 3253ms max |
| Unrelated navigation during them | **500ms** (78ms idle) |

In CI, where the browser, database and chat service share two vCPUs, that contention aborted a navigation outright and failed `browse.spec.ts` on #251 — `page.goto: net::ERR_ABORTED` after a 30s timeout. A first-time visitor gets the same thing, once; the cache hides it on every later visit, which is why nothing had caught it.

**So the defect is the count, not the cost per image.** Roughly 15 of the 18 were for cards nobody had scrolled to.

## What this does

An `IntersectionObserver` with a 1200px margin decides when a listing image is fetched.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Requests, 390x844 | 9 | **6** |
| Requests, 1440x900 | 18 | **9** |
| Deepest speculative fetch | 4.3 viewports | **1.4 viewports** |
| Navigation during in-flight jobs | 500ms | **121ms** |
| Document height | 5038px | 5038px |
| CLS | — | **0.000** |

**1200px, not 600.** The margin buys `1200 / v` seconds of lead at scroll speed `v`. At 600 with a 1000ms optimisation, 14 of 20 cards were still grey as they entered the viewport; on a phone at 2343ms, 14 never decoded while on screen at all.

**The first two categories stay eager and server-rendered.** A deferred image cannot be requested until the component hydrates — measured at +237ms unthrottled but **+2.0s at 6x CPU throttle**. Covering only the first category left six cards at 1440x2000 as empty boxes for that entire window before their request even started. With two, zero above-fold cards are still empty after 4s at every viewport tested up to 1440x2000.

**The reserved box and the loaded box are one element.** `next/image` renders with `color: transparent` and no background of its own, so hanging the tone on a placeholder that unmounts leaves the state a scrolling visitor actually sees — requested, not yet decoded — as a fully transparent gap. One element also keeps the document height identical and CLS at zero.

## What this gives up

Stated plainly, because they are real:

- **A deferred image is not in the server-rendered HTML.** `<noscript>` carries the unoptimised source for scripting-off, at roughly **12x the bytes** (5.1 MB against ~400 KB across the twenty cards). It does not cover scripting that loads and then *fails* — a blocked chunk leaves 17 of 20 cards as empty boxes. Filed as **#261**.
- **The box now assumes a square source.** The markup it replaces took its box from the source's own ratio. `config/catalogue_images.json` and `test_image_encoding.py` bound only the long edge, so a 1024x600 would letterbox with nothing turning red. All 853 catalogue sources are 1024x1024 today. Filed as **#262**.
- **`bg-zinc-200` is 1.22:1 and 1.15:1** against the two band colours, short of 1.4.11's 3:1. Deliberate: this is a transient state of an `alt=""` image whose card takes its name entirely from the link text, and a tone dark enough to pass would flash a heavy grey block on every ordinary load. Where that stops holding is the permanent case, which is #261.

## Scope

Home page only. The category grid is **worse** — measured at 21 of 21 requests on a 3965px document — and is filed as **#263**. It is out of this slice because its `priority={i < 3}` cutoff is an open question in #180, and answering both at once would tangle them. The spec header records that boundary.

## Verification

- **Red phase first.** The guard failed on the unfixed tree for the right reason: `18 optimiser requests for 20 cards before scrolling`, expected <= 8.
- `make -C apps/web ci` — exit 0: lint, both typechecks, **154/154** unit tests, production build.
- `make test-scripts` — 157/157.
- All **132 Playwright journeys** pass against a composed stack containing this change.
- Unit assertions demonstrated against deliberate mutations, each caught by exactly one: ignoring `eager`, moving the tone back onto an unmounting placeholder, and dropping the `rootMargin` argument.

`ui-review` exercised the rendered page at phone, tablet and desktop, at 1x and 2x, under injected optimiser latency and CPU throttling; its findings on the placeholder tone, the margin and the eager cutoff are what the three tuning decisions above came from. `verifier` caught that jsdom has no `IntersectionObserver`, which was breaking `page.test.tsx` — fixed with a polyfill beside the existing `matchMedia` one, deliberately one that observes and never fires, so a deferral test cannot pass without anything being deferred.

Refs #230, #261, #262, #263
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

input.new_string:
# Published host ports are deliberately off the defaults: 3100, 8100 and 55432
# rather than 3000, 8000 and 5432. Those three are the most contended ports a
# developer machine has -- every other Next app wants 3000, every other Python
# service 8000, every other Postgres 5432.
#
# This is not a tidiness preference. A collision on `db` is silent and
# destructive rather than loud: contoso's own container cannot bind, so it
# never starts, and every host-side Prisma command then resolves
# `localhost:5432` to the *other* project's server. Measured on a developer
# machine, a single `make migrate-deploy` created a full contoso schema inside
# an unrelated project's Postgres, and `make docker-init-fresh` would have
# seeded data into it. See #245.
#
# The left-hand number is the host's and is the only one that moved. Container
# ports stay at the defaults, so `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000` and the
# `db:5432` URLs below are unaffected -- they never leave the compose network.
services:
  web:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "3100:3000"

input.content:
"""Guard the published host ports and everything that has to agree with them.

A published port is not one number in one file. `docker-compose.yml` decides
what the host can reach, and at least six other places have to name the same
number or the stack is subtly wrong rather than obviously broken:

- `NEXTAUTH_URL` is the origin the browser is on, so it scopes the session
  cookie. Leave it behind and sign-in *succeeds*, then every authenticated
  request arrives without a cookie.
- `make e2e-smoke` and `scripts/e2e_smoke.py` probe literal addresses and
  cannot be aimed elsewhere, so a stale one reports a healthy stack that is
  not the stack, or a dead one that is running.
- CI's `E2E_BASE_URL` and Playwright's default aim the journeys.

None of those fails loudly on drift, which is why they are asserted together
here rather than left to whoever moves a port next.

The ports themselves are read out of `docker-compose.yml` rather than written
down here, so this measures *agreement* — the property that matters — instead
of restating one number in an eighth place. What is pinned is the separate
claim the move was made for: that none of them is the contended default.

`yaml` is deliberately not imported: CI's script-test job builds a bare
virtualenv, so a third-party import passes locally and fails there.
"""

import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
COMPOSE = REPO_ROOT / "docker-compose.yml"

# The ports every other project on a developer machine wants. Moving off these
# is the whole point of the arrangement this guards; see #245 for the incident.
CONTENDED = {"web": 3000, "chat": 8000, "db": 5432}


def read(relative: str) -> str:
    return (REPO_ROOT / relative).read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def published_ports() -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
    """`{service: (host_port, container_port)}` from the compose file.

    Slices on the top-level service keys rather than matching `"N:M"` anywhere,
    so a port that appears in a comment or an environment value cannot be
    mistaken for a published mapping.
    """
    lines = COMPOSE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    starts = [
        index
        for index, line in enumerate(lines)
        if re.fullmatch(r"  (\w[\w-]*):\s*", line)
    ]
    ports: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    for position, start in enumerate(starts):
        name = lines[start].strip().rstrip(":")
        end = starts[position + 1] if position + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        for line in lines[start:end]:
            match = re.fullmatch(r'\s*-\s*"(\d+):(\d+)"\s*', line)
            if match:
                ports[name] = (int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)))
                break
    return ports


class PublishedPortTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.ports = published_ports()

    def test_every_service_publishes_a_port(self):
        """Vacuity guard: a parse that finds nothing satisfies every claim below."""
        self.assertEqual(
            set(self.ports),
            {"web", "chat", "db"},
            f"parsed published ports {self.ports} out of {COMPOSE}",
        )

    def test_published_ports_are_off_the_contended_defaults(self):
        for service, default in CONTENDED.items():
            host, _ = self.ports[service]
            self.assertNotEqual(
                host,
                default,
                f"{service} publishes the contended default {default}. Another "
                f"project on the same machine takes it and this stack either "
                f"fails to bind or, for db, silently resolves to their server "
                f"(#245).",
            )

    def test_container_ports_stay_on_the_defaults(self):
        """The move is host-side only.

        Container ports are what `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000` and the
        `db:5432` URLs inside the compose network resolve to. Moving one of
        those breaks service-to-service traffic while every host-side check
        here keeps passing, so it is asserted rather than assumed.
        """
        for service, default in CONTENDED.items():
            _, container = self.ports[service]
            self.assertEqual(
                container,
                default,
                f"{service}'s container port moved to {container}; the compose "
                f"network addresses it by the default {default}",
            )

    def test_nextauth_url_names_the_published_web_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["web"]
        for source in ("docker-compose.yml", ".env.example"):
            content = read(source)
            match = re.search(r"NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:(\d+)", content)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"no NEXTAUTH_URL found in {source}")
            self.assertEqual(
                int(match.group(1)),
                host,
                f"{source} scopes the session cookie to a port the stack does "
                f"not answer on, so sign-in succeeds and every request after it "
                f"arrives unauthenticated",
            )

    def test_smoke_probes_the_published_ports(self):
        web, _ = self.ports["web"]
        chat, _ = self.ports["chat"]
        makefile = read("Makefile")
        self.assertIn(f'--web-url "http://127.0.0.1:{web}"', makefile)
        self.assertIn(f'--chat-url "http://127.0.0.1:{chat}"', makefile)

        smoke = read("scripts/e2e_smoke.py")
        self.assertIn(f'default="http://127.0.0.1:{web}"', smoke)
        self.assertIn(f'default="http://127.0.0.1:{chat}"', smoke)

    def test_journeys_are_aimed_at_the_published_web_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["web"]
        self.assertIn(f"E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:{host}", read(".github/workflows/ci.yml"))
        self.assertIn(
            f"'http://localhost:{host}'",
            read("apps/web/playwright.config.ts"),
        )

    def test_host_side_database_url_names_the_published_db_port(self):
        host, _ = self.ports["db"]
        for source in (".env.example", "services/chat/.env.example"):
            content = read(source)
            match = re.search(r"DATABASE_URL=postgresql://[^@]+@localhost:(\d+)/", content)
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"no host-side DATABASE_URL in {source}")
            self.assertEqual(
                int(match.group(1)),
                host,
                f"{source} points host-side Prisma at a port this stack does "
                f"not publish. On a machine where something else holds it, that "
                f"is another project's database (#245)",
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Break each coupled file on purpose; confirm the matching assertion fails.

Points every path constant the assertions dereference at a fixture tree, never
the checkout, per tests/scripts/AGENTS.md. `read()` resolves through REPO_ROOT
and `published_ports()` through COMPOSE, so both are rebound.
"""

import shutil
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from tests.scripts import test_published_ports as mod

REAL = Path('/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso')
FIXTURES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'portfix'

COUPLED = [
    'docker-compose.yml',
    '.env.example',
    'services/chat/.env.example',
    'Makefile',
    'scripts/e2e_smoke.py',
    '.github/workflows/ci.yml',
    'apps/web/playwright.config.ts',
]


def build_tree(case: str) -> Path:
    root = FIXTURES / case
    if root.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(root)
    for rel in COUPLED:
        dest = root / rel
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy(REAL / rel, dest)
    return root


def run(case: str, mutate=None):
    root = build_tree(case)
    if mutate:
        mutate(root)
    mod.REPO_ROOT = root
    mod.COMPOSE = root / 'docker-compose.yml'

    suite = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(mod.PublishedPortTests)
    with open('/dev/null', 'w') as devnull:
        result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=0, stream=devnull).run(suite)
    failed = {t.id().rsplit('.', 1)[-1] for t, _ in result.failures + result.errors}
    print(f"\n=== {case} ===")
    print(f"  fixture: {root}")
    print(f"  failing: {sorted(failed) or 'none'}")
    return failed


def edit(root: Path, rel: str, old: str, new: str):
    p = root / rel
    s = p.read_text()
    assert old in s, f"{rel}: {old!r} not present"
    p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))


print('Baseline: the real coupled files, copied unchanged.')
assert run('baseline') == set(), 'healthy fixture should be clean'

print('\nMistake 1: web moved back to the contended default 3000.')
f = run('contended', lambda r: edit(r, 'docker-compose.yml', '"3100:3000"', '"3000:3000"'))
assert 'test_published_ports_are_off_the_contended_defaults' in f, f

print('\nMistake 2: the container port moved instead of the host port.')
f = run('container-moved', lambda r: edit(r, 'docker-compose.yml', '"8100:8000"', '"8100:8100"'))
assert 'test_container_ports_stay_on_the_defaults' in f, f

print('\nMistake 3: web port moved, NEXTAUTH_URL left behind (silent auth break).')
def only_port(r):
    edit(r, 'docker-compose.yml', '"3100:3000"', '"3200:3000"')
f = run('nextauth-stale', only_port)
assert 'test_nextauth_url_names_the_published_web_port' in f, f
assert 'test_smoke_probes_the_published_ports' in f, f
assert 'test_journeys_are_aimed_at_the_published_web_port' in f, f

print('\nMistake 4: chat port moved, smoke probe left behind.')
f = run('smoke-stale', lambda r: edit(r, 'docker-compose.yml', '"8100:8000"', '"8200:8000"'))
assert 'test_smoke_probes_the_published_ports' in f, f
assert 'test_nextauth_url_names_the_published_web_port' not in f, f

print('\nMistake 5: db port moved, host-side DATABASE_URL left behind.')
f = run('db-stale', lambda r: edit(r, 'docker-compose.yml', '"55432:5432"', '"55433:5432"'))
assert 'test_host_side_database_url_names_the_published_db_port' in f, f

print('\nMistake 6: compose ports removed entirely, which would empty every claim.')
def strip_ports(r):
    p = r / 'docker-compose.yml'
    kept = [l for l in p.read_text().splitlines() if not l.strip().startswith('- "')]
    p.write_text('\n'.join(kept))
f = run('no-ports', strip_ports)
assert 'test_every_service_publishes_a_port' in f, f

print('\nAll demonstrations behaved as claimed.')

Found while verifying the hybrid dev flow for the published-port move.

## What happens

Running `make dev-web` (`next dev`, Next 16.3.0) appends this to `apps/web/AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->

# This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` ... before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.

<!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
```

Reproduced by starting the dev server once. The generator is `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`.

## Why this is worth a decision rather than a shrug

`AGENTS.md` is not an ordinary file in this repository. The root one opens with **"`AGENTS.md` is the canonical format for agent instructions"** and the whole pointer-file discipline — `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` carrying no instructions of their own, enforced by `make agent-docs-check` — exists to keep exactly one authority for what an agent is told to do.

A framework appending instructions to that file, on every `next dev`, from `node_modules`, is a third party writing into the governance surface. The content is reasonable; that is not the point. The mechanism means:

- Anyone running `make dev-web` gets a dirty tree, and the dirt is *inside* the instruction file, where the diff is easy to wave through.
- The instructions change when the `next` version changes, without anyone reviewing them.
- The block's own text lobbies for its inclusion: *"committing it with your work keeps the tree clean."*

## What it does not do

`make agent-docs-check` and `make docs-check` both **pass** with the block present — measured. `check_agent_docs.py` guards pointer files against gaining content; it does not police additions to `AGENTS.md` itself. So nothing turns red, which is the reason this can drift in unnoticed.

## Options

1. **Commit it**, and accept that a `next` upgrade can silently rewrite part of the agent instructions. Cheapest, and the block's own advice.
2. **Suppress it.** Worth checking whether the generator honours an opt-out before assuming it does not.
3. **Commit it but guard it** — pin the block's content in `tests/scripts/test_agent_definitions.py` or similar, so a `next` upgrade that changes what agents are told fails a check and gets read.

Option 3 is the one that matches how this repository treats its other unheld assumptions. It is a decision about what agents are instructed to do, so it is the repository owner's rather than something to settle inside an unrelated branch.

## Related

- #260 — `next-env.d.ts` churn from the same source. Now slightly worse than that issue records: `next build` writes `./.next/types/routes.d.ts` while `next dev` writes `./.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts` plus a `root-params` line, so the two commands fight over the file and whichever ran last wins.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

| `.env.example` `CHAT_ENDPOINT` 8100 → 8000 | **no failure** |

def ports_in(value: str) -> list[int]:
    """Every host port a value names, across a comma-separated list.

    `urlsplit` rather than a regex for the port: a DSN's password may start
    with digits (`postgres:5up3r@localhost:55432`), and a non-greedy pattern
    stops at those and reports a port that appears nowhere.
    """
    found = []
    for element in value.split(","):
        element = element.strip()
        if not element:
            continue
        try:
            port = urlsplit(element).port
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if port is not None:
            found.append(port)
    return found


def stale_port_keys(env: dict[str, str], ports: dict[str, int]) -> list[str]:
    """Keys in `env` whose host port disagrees with what compose publishes.

    A value naming several origins is stale only when *none* of them is the
    published port, so adding a second origin does not start warning on the
    order it was written in.
    """
    stale = []
    for key, service in PORT_BEARING_KEYS.items():
        value = env.get(key)
        if not value:
            continue
        # ALLOWED_ORIGINS names the *web* origin the browser is on, even though
        # it configures chat.
        expected = ports.get("web" if service == "chat_origin" else service)
        if expected is None:
            continue
        found = ports_in(value)
        if found and expected not in found:
            named = ", ".join(f":{port}" for port in found)
            stale.append(f"{key} names {named}, compose publishes :{expected}")
    return stale

"""Guard `agent_doctor`'s port-drift detection.

`.env` is not tracked, so moving a published port in the repository leaves
every existing one behind. The keys that carry a port fail by *reaching
something else* rather than by erroring — `CHAT_ENDPOINT` posts the request and
its API key to whatever now owns the old port, and `services/chat/.env`'s
`DATABASE_URL` runs hand-written asyncpg queries against whatever owns 5432.
That is what this detection exists for, and it is worth testing because it is
the only thing standing between a stale file and a silent wrong target.

Two shapes of assertion here:

- Table tests over `stale_port_keys`, which is a pure function of two dicts.
  These are what catch parsing mistakes; the first version of it read a DSN's
  digit-leading password as the port.
- One vacuity assertion that `published_ports()` parses the real compose file
  non-empty. That is the important one: this parser **fails open**. If the
  compose format drifts, it returns `{}`, every key is skipped, and the warning
  silently stops existing rather than going red. `test_published_ports.py`
  carries a second copy of the same parser whose failure is loud, so without
  this assertion the two could diverge with only the quiet one left standing.
"""

import importlib.util
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def load_agent_doctor():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "agent_doctor", REPO_ROOT / "scripts/agent_doctor.py"
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


doctor = load_agent_doctor()

PORTS = {"web": 3100, "chat": 8100, "db": 55432}


class PortsInTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reads_the_port_not_a_digit_leading_password(self):
        """The mistake the first implementation made.

        A non-greedy `://.*?:(\\d+)` stops at the password and reports `:5`,
        which appears nowhere in the value.
        """
        dsn = "REDACTED"
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(dsn), [55432])

    def test_reads_every_element_of_a_comma_separated_list(self):
        origins = "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3100"
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(origins), [5173, 3100])

    def test_a_value_naming_no_port_yields_none(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("REDACTED"), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("https://example.com"), [])

    def test_an_unparseable_value_is_skipped_rather_than_raising(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in("http://localhost:not-a-port"), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.ports_in(""), [])


class StalePortKeyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_stale_file_names_every_drifted_key(self):
        env = {
            "NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3000",
            "CHAT_ENDPOINT": "http://localhost:8000/api/create_response",
            "ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:3000",
            "DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED",
        }
        stale = doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS)
        self.assertEqual(len(stale), 3)
        self.assertTrue(any("NEXTAUTH_URL names :3000" in item for item in stale))
        self.assertTrue(any("CHAT_ENDPOINT names :8000" in item for item in stale))
        # Already migrated, so it must not be reported.
        self.assertFalse(any("DATABASE_URL" in item for item in stale))

    def test_a_current_file_reports_nothing(self):
        env = {
            "NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3100",
            "CHAT_ENDPOINT": "http://localhost:8100/api/create_response",
            "ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:3100",
            "DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED",
        }
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])

    def test_a_list_containing_the_published_port_is_not_stale(self):
        """Order must not decide the verdict.

        Warning on the first element alone makes the check sensitive to where
        someone happened to add a second origin.
        """
        env = {"ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3100"}
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])

    def test_a_list_containing_none_of_them_is_stale(self):
        env = {"ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:3000"}
        self.assertEqual(len(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS)), 1)

    def test_absent_keys_and_absent_ports_are_skipped(self):
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys({}, PORTS), [])
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys({"FOO": "bar"}, PORTS), [])
        # No compose ports parsed: nothing to compare against, so nothing said.
        self.assertEqual(
            doctor.stale_port_keys({"NEXTAUTH_URL": "http://localhost:3000"}, {}),
            [],
        )

    def test_a_portless_value_is_not_reported(self):
        env = {"DATABASE_URL": "REDACTED"}
        self.assertEqual(doctor.stale_port_keys(env, PORTS), [])


class PublishedPortParseTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_real_compose_file_parses_non_empty(self):
        """The fail-open guard.

        Every assertion above is about a function that is only reached when
        this parser returns something. If compose's formatting drifts past the
        parser, it returns `{}` and the whole check quietly becomes a no-op —
        so this is asserted against the real file rather than a fixture.
        """
        ports = doctor.published_ports()
        self.assertEqual(
            set(ports),
            {"web", "chat", "db"},
            f"parsed {ports} from the real docker-compose.yml; the drift "
            f"warning is a no-op whenever this is empty",
        )
        for service, port in ports.items():
            self.assertIsInstance(port, int, f"{service} port is not an int")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

gh pr create --title "chore(compose): publish ports off the contended defaults" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes #245. Closes #240.

## Why

Another project on this machine wants 3000, 8000 and 5432 — and every developer machine has something that does.

The `db` collision is not a loud one. contoso's container cannot bind, so it never starts, and every host-side Prisma command then resolves `localhost:5432` to **the other project's server**. #245 measured it: a single `make migrate-deploy` created a full contoso schema inside an unrelated project's Postgres, and `make docker-init-fresh` would have seeded data into it.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| web | `3000:3000` | **`3100:3000`** |
| chat | `8000:8000` | **`8100:8000`** |
| db | `5432:5432` | **`55432:5432`** |

**Only the host side moved.** Container ports stay at the defaults, so `CHAT_ENDPOINT=http://chat:8000` and the `db:5432` URLs inside the compose network are untouched.

## A published port is not one number

The places coupled to it fail by *reaching something else* rather than by erroring, so they move together:

- **`NEXTAUTH_URL`** — what NextAuth builds absolute redirect URLs from. A stale one lands **sign-out** on a dead port. Not sign-in: `login/page.tsx` passes `redirect: false` and navigates itself. And not the session cookie, which is not isolated by port at all.
- **The smoke probes** in `Makefile` and `scripts/e2e_smoke.py` are literal and cannot be aimed elsewhere, so a stale one reports a healthy stack that is not the stack, or a dead one that is running.
- **`CHAT_ENDPOINT`** — `route.ts` reads it with no fallback and posts with `CHAT_API_KEY` attached.
- Plus `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, CI's `E2E_BASE_URL`, Playwright's default, CI's chat health probes, and the docs and agent runbooks.

`tests/scripts/test_published_ports.py` reads the ports out of compose and asserts the rest agree, rather than writing 3100 down a ninth time. Nine assertions, demonstrated against a fixture tree for every drift mode including **moving the container port instead of the host port**.

## The dev server moved too

`apps/web/package.json` is now `next dev -p 3100`. Leaving it on 3000 would have made every file agree while contoso still held the port this change exists to give up — a fix that passes its own guard and solves nothing. Verified live: the dev server answers on 3100 and **3000 answers nothing**.

## Existing `.env` files cannot be migrated by a commit

Neither `.env` nor `services/chat/.env` is tracked, so this change cannot fix them — and a stale `CHAT_ENDPOINT` posts the request and its API key to whatever now owns 8000.

`make agent-doctor` now names every drifted key in **both** files. The chat one matters more: it is what `load_dotenv()` finds when the service runs from its own directory, and those queries are hand-written **asyncpg rather than Prisma**, so a stale port runs raw SQL against someone else's database. Both READMEs carry a migration note, placed in the flow that actually reads each file.

## Also fixes a false claim

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` said `E2E_BASE_URL` must match `NEXTAUTH_URL` "or the session cookie is set for a different origin". Cookies are not port-scoped (RFC 6265 §8.5), and #240 measured a remapped stack signing in fine. Corrected there and in the four places I had initially repeated the same misconception.

## Deliberately unchanged

Container-internal ports: `.devcontainer` `forwardPorts`, `Dockerfile` `EXPOSE 3000`/`PORT=3000`, `apps/web`'s `start` script. Local processes: chat's `uvicorn --port 8000`. Different things entirely: `docs/DATABASE.md` and `dev_db_proxy.sh` (Cloud SQL Auth Proxy), Terraform's Cloud Run `container_port`, and fixture DSNs in tests.

## Verification

Five rounds. `make ci` exit 0; `make test-scripts` **177/177**; the full **130-journey** suite against a composed stack on the new ports; `make e2e-smoke` passing; `auth.spec.ts` 5/5 — which proves the auth coupling end to end rather than merely consistent; `make docker-init-fresh` correctly deriving 55432 and seeding the right database; hybrid `next dev` verified live.

## Filed, not fixed here

#262 (nothing enforces square catalogue images), #263 (the category grid's own optimiser contention), #265 (`next dev` writes into `apps/web/AGENTS.md`), #266 (`scripts/*.py` outside every lint gate), #267 (does the devcontainer still work?).

Refs #245, #240
EOF

"""Guard the local development surface against defects that pass silently.

The three things asserted here had one property in common before they were
fixed: none of them could fail. `sync-env`'s whole body sat behind a path test
that was always false, so it exited 0 and printed nothing on every run for as
long as it has existed. A `docker-compose.override.yml` that is not ignored
looks exactly like one that is, until someone commits it. A `prisma migrate
dev` with no `--name` looks fine until the schema has actually changed, and
then it blocks on a prompt no non-TTY can answer and exits 130 — a
cancellation, not a missing argument.

So each assertion here measures the effect rather than the text:

- the `sync-env` source path is **resolved** from the directory the recipe runs
  in and compared to the repo root, because `../.env` and `../../.env` are both
  plausible strings and only one of them names a file that exists;
- `git check-ignore` is asked whether the override is ignored, rather than
  `.gitignore` being grepped for a line that could be anchored wrong, negated
  later, or shadowed;
- every `prisma migrate dev` in tracked documentation is checked, not the one
  file that happened to be wrong.

Not covered: the unsupported `eslint` key removed from `next.config.js` at the
same time. Asserting a key is absent is a declaration check, and the thing that
actually reports it is `next build`, which CI already runs — the key never
enforced anything, since lint runs as its own step.
"""

import re
import subprocess
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WEB_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "apps/web"
WEB_MAKEFILE = WEB_DIR / "Makefile"
OVERRIDE = "docker-compose.override.yml"


def sync_env_sources() -> list[str]:
    """Every path the `sync-env` recipe reads, as written in the Makefile."""
    lines = WEB_MAKEFILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    body: list[str] = []
    inside = False
    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith("sync-env:"):
            inside = True
            continue
        if inside:
            # A recipe line is tab-indented; anything else ends the target.
            if not line.startswith("\t"):
                break
            body.append(line)
    return re.findall(r"(\.\.[./]*\.env)", "\n".join(body))


def tracked_docs() -> list[Path]:
    listed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files", "*.md"],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return [REPO_ROOT / name for name in listed.stdout.split()]


class SyncEnvTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_recipe_reads_a_path(self):
        """Vacuity guard: an empty parse satisfies the resolution check below."""
        self.assertTrue(
            sync_env_sources(),
            f"parsed no .env path out of sync-env in {WEB_MAKEFILE}",
        )

    def test_every_source_resolves_to_the_repo_root_env(self):
        """Resolved, not matched.

        The recipe runs with `apps/web` as its working directory, so the string
        is only correct relative to that. `../.env` resolves to `apps/.env`,
        which has never existed — and because the recipe guards on `-f`, that
        wrong path and an absent root `.env` produce identical output.
        """
        for source in sync_env_sources():
            resolved = (WEB_DIR / source).resolve()
            self.assertEqual(
                resolved,
                (REPO_ROOT / ".env").resolve(),
                f"sync-env reads {source!r}, which from {WEB_DIR.name} resolves "
                f"to {resolved} rather than the repo root .env. The `-f` guard "
                f"makes that silent (#212).",
            )


class ComposeOverrideTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_local_compose_override_is_ignored(self):
        """Asked of git, not of `.gitignore`.

        `docker compose` auto-loads this file, so a committed one applies to
        everyone and to CI without being asked for. Grepping `.gitignore` would
        pass on a pattern that is anchored wrong or negated further down; git
        is the tool that decides.
        """
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "check-ignore", "-q", OVERRIDE],
            cwd=REPO_ROOT,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            result.returncode,
            0,
            f"git does not ignore {OVERRIDE}, so a machine-local override can "
            f"be committed and will then apply to everyone and to CI (#247)",
        )


class MigrateCommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_documented_migrate_dev_commands_name_the_migration(self):
        offenders = []
        seen = 0
        for doc in tracked_docs():
            for line in doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
                if "prisma migrate dev" not in line:
                    continue
                seen += 1
                if "--name" not in line:
                    offenders.append(f"{doc.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}: {line.strip()}")
        # Vacuity: if no document mentions the command, the loop above proves
        # nothing and this test would pass on a docs tree that lost it.
        self.assertGreater(seen, 0, "no tracked document shows `prisma migrate dev`")
        self.assertEqual(
            offenders,
            [],
            "`prisma migrate dev` without --name stops at an interactive prompt "
            "once the schema has changed, which a non-TTY cannot answer: it "
            "exits 130 with no migration created, and reads as a cancellation "
            "rather than a missing argument (#246). Offenders: "
            + "; ".join(offenders),
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def build(case, makefile_body, docs, gitignore):
    root = FIX / case
    if root.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(root)
    (root / 'apps/web').mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / 'docs').mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / 'apps/web/Makefile').write_text(makefile_body)
    for name, text in docs.items():
        (root / name).write_text(text)
    (root / '.gitignore').write_text(gitignore)
    subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q'], cwd=root, check=True)
    subprocess.run(['git', 'add', '-A'], cwd=root, check=True,
                   capture_output=True)
    return root


GOOD_MAKE = "sync-env: ## Sync\n\t@if [ -f ../../.env ]; then cp ../../.env .env; fi\n\ndev:\n\techo hi\n"
BAD_MAKE = "sync-env: ## Sync\n\t@if [ -f ../.env ]; then cp ../.env .env; fi\n\ndev:\n\techo hi\n"
NO_PATH_MAKE = "sync-env: ## Sync\n\t@true\n\ndev:\n\techo hi\n"

GOOD_IGNORE = "/docker-compose.override.yml\n"
BAD_IGNORE = "node_modules/\n"

class SyncEnvExecutionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Run the real recipe, rather than reading it.

    The parse above catches the class of bug that was actually there — a path
    correct from the wrong directory. It cannot catch the next one: a quoting
    mistake, a `make` variable that expands to nothing, a `cp` whose argument
    order slipped. Those all leave a recipe that reads correctly and copies
    nothing, which is precisely the failure `sync-env` already had once.

    `apps/web/Makefile` has no `include` and no state outside itself, so it can
    be copied into a fixture tree and invoked there. Nothing here touches the
    checkout.
    """

    def run_sync_env(self, root: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        web = root / "apps/web"
        web.mkdir(parents=True)
        shutil.copy(WEB_MAKEFILE, web / "Makefile")
        return subprocess.run(
            ["make", "sync-env"],
            cwd=web,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )

    def test_it_copies_the_repo_root_env(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            (root / ".env").write_text("MARKER=from-repo-root\n", encoding="utf-8")

            result = self.run_sync_env(root)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)

            copied = root / "apps/web/.env"
            self.assertTrue(
                copied.exists(),
                "sync-env exited 0 without copying anything — which is exactly "
                "how the `../.env` bug looked for as long as it existed (#212)",
            )
            self.assertEqual(copied.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "MARKER=from-repo-root\n")

    def test_it_stays_quiet_when_there_is_no_root_env(self):
        """The `-f` guard's legitimate case, which is why it is there.

        CI creates no `.env`, so the target has to be a no-op rather than a
        failure. Asserted so that a future fix for the silence above cannot
        turn this into a hard error.
        """
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            result = self.run_sync_env(root)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
            self.assertFalse((root / "apps/web/.env").exists())

`apps/web/Makefile` ran `cp ../.env .env`. The recipe's working directory is `apps/web`, so `../.env` is **`apps/.env`** — a path that has never existed, because `apps/` holds only `web/`.

The `-f` guard is what made it silent. The whole body sat behind an always-false condition, so it exited 0 and printed nothing on every run since it was written, and a missing root `.env` looked identical to a wrong path.

So `make dev-web` has never handed the dev server a `DATABASE_URL`, a `NEXTAUTH_URL` or a `CHAT_ENDPOINT`. Measured before and after:

```
$ ls apps/web/.env
ls: cannot access 'apps/web/.env': No such file or directory
$ make -C apps/web sync-env && ls apps/web/.env
-rw-rw-r-- 1 ... 2659 apps/web/.env        # byte-identical to the root .env
```

## #247 — the compose override was not ignored

`docker compose` auto-loads `docker-compose.override.yml`, so a committed one applies to everyone and to CI *without being asked for* — worse than having no override, and it is the standard way to carry a port remap around a collision on a shared machine.

## #246 — the last bare `prisma migrate dev`

Once the schema has actually changed, that command stops at an interactive prompt no non-TTY can answer: exit 130, no migration created, and it reads as a cancellation rather than a missing argument.

Not merely redundant. `next lint` was removed in Next 16, the option is absent from the installed config schema, and there is no ESLint invocation left in the build. Lint runs as its own CI step and is unchanged. Measured: **1 unrecognized-key warning on `main`, 0 on this branch.**

A second test asserts it stays a silent no-op with no root `.env`, which is the `-f` guard's legitimate case in CI. A separate parse resolves the source path from the recipe's working directory, so the failure message names *why*.
- **Asks git** whether the override is ignored rather than grepping `.gitignore`. That also covers a force-added override, since `check-ignore` reports a tracked path as not-ignored.

This is what makes `apps/web/.env` start existing on contributors' machines for the first time. It is gitignored by the existing bare `.env` pattern and is the target's stated purpose, but the footprint change is real, not just a bug fix.

Three spellings of the same placeholder across three documents — `your_migration_name` in `README.md`, `<migration-name>` in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/DATABASE.md`, `add-order-status` in `AGENTS.md`. Cosmetic, and outside a diff about commands that cannot run.

Measured on the running stack at 834x1112:

```
cards intersecting viewport: 0,1,2,3

  card 3: top=861 bottom=1254   (deferred)
```

1112 − 861 = **251px of card 3 is on screen at entry** — exactly the figure the pre-existing comment at line 99 records ("card 3 is eager and card 4 is lazy, both 251px above the fold"). The served HTML confirms only three real `<img>` remain (`curl` returns 21 `<img` of which 18 are inside `<noscript>`, and 3 preload links).

Time until card 3 has an `<img>` at all, at 834x1112:

| CPU throttle | FCP | card 3 img present | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x | 200ms | 445ms | ~245ms |
| 4x | 432ms | 1587ms | ~1155ms |

Before this change card 3 was a server-rendered `<img loading="lazy">` inside Chrome's ~3900px threshold, so its request started at parse. Now it starts after hydration.

At 1440x900 cards 3, 4 and 5 are also 63px on screen — marginal, but the same mechanism.

Concrete scenario: a visitor on a tablet, or any mid-range phone in landscape hitting the `sm` breakpoint, lands on `/products/category/tents` and sees a grey `bg-gray-200` box where a quarter of a product card should be, for a quarter-second on a fast device and over two seconds on a slow one.

It looks close to free: those cards already sit inside the 1200px `rootMargin` at every viewport in the table, so they are already in the measured 12/8 counts and the prop only moves them from post-hydration into the HTML. Only the phone count would move (4 → 6, adding cards 4 and 5), well under `MAX_INITIAL_CATEGORY_REQUESTS`. cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso && gh issue create --title "The image optimiser can wedge on specific variants until the container is restarted" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Found while verifying #263. Recorded because it cost a long misdiagnosis and would cost the next person the same.

## What happened

`e2e/image-delivery.spec.ts › the category grid image is sized to its box` failed twice at its 240s ceiling, on a quiet machine, alone. Its historical duration is ~58s.

The cause was not the test. At 390x900 the page never reached `readyState: complete`, and three optimiser requests sat in flight indefinitely:

```
still in flight after 12s:
  12035ms image /_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fproducts%2Ftents%2F21%2Fmain.webp&w=384&q=75
  12036ms image /_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fproducts%2Ftents%2F24%2Fmain.webp&w=384&q=75
  12035ms image /_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fproducts%2Ftents%2F25%2Fmain.webp&w=384&q=75
```

Outside the browser, the same three returned **nothing at all**:

```
product 21 w=384: HTTP 000 in 40.002820s     <- curl --max-time 40, no response
product 24 w=384: HTTP 000 in 40.001979s
product 25 w=384: HTTP 000 in 40.002537s
```

While, on the same process, at the same moment:

```
product 21 w=640:            HTTP 200 in 0.005171s
/images/1/242e7165-....webp  w=384: HTTP 200 in 0.146848s
```

So it is not the width, and not the image — it is a *specific (image, width) variant* that stops responding while its neighbours are served in milliseconds. No error appeared in `docker compose logs web`.

## What cleared it

`docker compose restart web`. Immediately afterwards:

```
product 21 w=384: HTTP 200 in 0.378816s
product 24 w=384: HTTP 200 in 0.163032s
product 25 w=384: HTTP 200 in 0.143939s
```

and the failing test passed in **55.1s**, against its ~58s historical baseline. The full journey suite then passed 134/134.

## What I contaminated, and what survives it

Two things I did during the investigation muddy this, and both are worth stating:

1. I ran `rm -rf .next/cache/images` **inside the running container**, which may have left the optimiser holding cache state for entries that no longer existed.
2. For a period I ran two Playwright suites against the same stack concurrently.

Neither explains the original failures, which happened **before** both. But they mean the exact trigger is not established.

What survives: a long-lived optimiser process reached a state where specific variants never respond, no log line was emitted, and only a restart recovered it.

## Why it matters beyond a flaky test

The failure mode is indefinite hang rather than error. A visitor hitting a wedged variant gets an image that never arrives and a `load` event that never fires. #230 established this optimiser is already the contended resource on these pages; this is a sharper version of the same theme — not slow, but stopped.

## Worth investigating

- Whether concurrent identical requests for one variant can deadlock on Next's in-flight dedupe.
- Whether cache-directory mutation under a running server is the trigger, which would make it self-inflicted here but still a fragility.
- Whether a request timeout in front of the optimiser would turn an indefinite hang into a failed image, which is a much better failure.

## Related

- #230 — the optimiser as a contended resource on the home page.
- #263 — the change being verified when this surfaced; it is not the cause, confirmed by the same test passing at 55.1s on a restarted container with the change in place.
EOF

`3` is the `priority` cutoff. Cards 0-2 carry an `<img>` no matter what `eager` is set to, because `priority` implies eager inside the component. Closes #263. The sequel to #230.

## What was wrong

The category grid asked the optimiser for **21 of its 21** images before any scrolling, on a **3965px** document. That is worse than the home page was: Chrome's `loading="lazy"` threshold measured ~3900px, so on this surface it swallowed the entire page rather than four viewports of it.

| viewport | before | after | document |
|---|---|---|---|
| phone 390×844 | 7 / 21 | **6 / 21** | 10690px (unchanged) |
| tablet 834×1112 | 16 / 21 | **8 / 21** | 6015px (unchanged) |
| desktop 1440×900 | **21 / 21** | **12 / 21** | 3965px (unchanged) |

Both measured on the same composed stack, baseline first.

## The shape

The mechanism moves out of `ListingImage` into **`DeferredImage`**, which renders into a box the **caller** owns. The category card already has one — `aspect-square … bg-gray-200` — and shares it with the "No image available" empty state, so a component bringing its own would nest two boxes around one image. `ListingImage` is now the home grid's box composing it, and its five tests pass untouched.

## Two cutoffs, deliberately not one

`priority={i < 3}` is **preserved exactly**. Its comment argues it from largest-contentful-paint medians (2892ms against 4048 at 1440), and `priority` now implies eager inside the component — a preloaded image that is also deferred is a contradiction.

`eager={i < 6}` answers a different question: not which card paints *last*, but which cards a visitor is *already looking at*. At `sm` the grid is two columns, so card 3 opens the second row and sits **251px on screen** — and a deferred card cannot be requested until hydration, measured at **245ms** unthrottled and **2385ms at 6× CPU**.

Six rather than four because the taller desktops decide it: that second row measures **243px at 1440×1080** and **363px at 1920×1200**, where four would fill card 3 and leave 4 and 5 grey beside it — ragged within a single row, which reads worse than a row that is uniformly not there yet. The price is two extra requests on phone, below the fold.

## The guard that holds it

`every card on the first screen is server-rendered, not waiting on hydration`.

The request-count journeys bound from *above*, so narrowing `eager` makes every one of them **greener** while putting cards back behind hydration. Demonstrated with a container rebuild in each direction — with `eager` removed:

```
✓ the home page does not optimise every card before it is scrolled to
✓ the category grid does not optimise every card before it is scrolled to
✘ every card on the first screen is server-rendered, not waiting on hydration
✓ the category grid still preloads its first row
✓ scrolling loads the images that were deferred
```

Four green, one red. That asymmetry is how the hole got in during review.

It blocks script chunks rather than disabling JavaScript. **`javaScriptEnabled: false` is worse than useless here**: with scripting off, `<noscript>` becomes live DOM, so every card reports an image whether or not anything was server-rendered — 21 against 6. It also asserts it *blocked* something, because a glob that stops matching fails open; pointing it at a path Next does not use leaves every assertion passing.

## Verification

`make -C apps/web ci` exit 0. **Full journey suite 135/135.** 9 component tests. `ui-review` at phone/tablet/desktop, 1× and 2×: placeholder 1.19:1 against the page versus the home grid's 1.22:1, `object-cover` cards pixel-identical to the untouched priority cards used as an in-page control, CLS 0, 0 of 21 grey on entry at 800px/s under 150ms and 1000ms injected latency, LCP 176/192/224ms still landing on a first-row image.

## Two corrections worth recording

- `ui-review` reported 2× density was not served, inferring ~398px sources. It is served: sources are 1024×1024 and `w=828` returns a genuine 828×828, confirmed by decoding the VP8 bitstreams. `398px` appears verbatim in the page's `sizes` string, which is the likely reading.
- Mid-review the suite failed twice at a 240s ceiling and I spent a long time assuming this change caused it. It did not — the optimiser had **wedged**, returning nothing for 40s on specific variants while neighbours served in milliseconds. A restart cleared it and the test returned to 55.1s against its ~58s baseline. Filed as **#270**, with my own contamination disclosed.

## Filed, not fixed here

#270 (the optimiser wedge), #271 (the header avatar preloading on every signed-in page, which competes with the LCP preloads this page tunes).

Refs #263
EOF

Found by `ui-review` on `perf/prioritise-lcp-images` (#169). A known, measured consequence of the cutoff that PR chose, filed rather than fixed because the alternatives are worse on the numbers.

## What it looks like

`priority={i < 3}` preloads the first three cards. At **834×1112** the grid is two columns, so cards 3 and 4 sit side by side with **251px of each above the fold** — and card 3 is index 2 (eager) while card 4 is index 3 (lazy).

Median load completion over three throttled runs (1.6 Mbps / 150 ms RTT / 4× CPU):

```
card 3 (eager)  1295 ms
card 4 (lazy)   3980 ms
```

A **2.7-second gap between two adjacent, equally visible cards in the same row.** The rendered filmstrip at 2200 ms shows three tents painted and a bare grey box beside the third.

At 1440 the equivalent band is cards 4–6 with 63px visible, and they are uniformly late, which reads as "there is more below" rather than as something broken. At 390 there is no artifact — nothing below card 1 is on screen.

## Why #169 shipped it anyway

`priority` cannot vary by viewport, so one cutoff serves all three layouts. Measured LCP by cutoff, median of 7:

| width | n=0 | n=1 | n=2 | **n=3** | n=6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 390 | 1540 | **736** | 744 | 748 | 840 |
| 834 | 2380 | **1404** | 1480 | 1488 | 1588 |
| 1440 | 2836 | 2972 | 1816 | **1788** | 1900 |

Summed regret against the best value at each width: n=1 costs 1184 ms, n=2 costs 112, **n=3 costs 96**, n=6 costs 400. So 3 is the best available single number, and 6 — which would cover the visible rows at 1440 — is worse everywhere.

Note n=1 is *worse than doing nothing* at 1440.

## Options

1. **Accept it.** The artifact is at one breakpoint band, it is a delay rather than a defect, and CLS is 0.0000 throughout because the `aspect-square` wrapper reserves the box. This is where #169 left it.
2. **A hand-rolled responsive preload.** `<link rel="preload" as="image" media="...">` can vary by viewport where `priority` cannot. Measured ceiling on the gain: **84 ms at 834 and 12 ms at 390**. Real machinery for very little.
3. **Cut at 4.** Untested. It would pair cards 3 and 4 correctly at 834 and cost phones a third off-screen preload; the n=6 row suggests the cost curve is already rising.

(1) unless someone finds the tablet band jarring in practice.

## Worth knowing

`next/image`'s `priority` sets no `fetchpriority` in Next 16.2 — it only flips `loading` and emits a preload link. So preloaded cards compete with the LCP element on equal terms, which is the mechanism behind both the n=1 regression and this artifact.

What #263 plausibly *did* change is the contention: index 3 now competes with 7 other requests at tablet instead of 18. So the gap may have narrowed — and the n=3 cutoff was chosen when 21 images competed.
