gh issue comment 180 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Re-measured after #263, and option 3 is now tested

#263 deferred the category grid's off-screen images, which changes the conditions this issue was measured under: the surface used to fetch 21 images at parse and now fetches 8 at tablet. That is a different amount of contention, so the numbers here needed re-taking. Same method as the original — 1.6 Mbps / 150ms RTT / 4x CPU, medians of 5.

### The artifact is improved, not gone

At 834x1112, cards 3 and 4 (indices 2 and 3), both 251px above the fold:

| | this issue (before) | after #263 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| card 3, index 2, `priority` | 1295ms | 1317ms |
| card 4, index 3, lazy | 3980ms | **2950ms** |
| **gap** | **2685ms** | **1633ms** |

So a second came off it, entirely from removing competition rather than from anything aimed at this. Two adjacent, equally visible cards in one row still arrive 1.6s apart, so the artifact this issue describes is still there.

At 1440 the 63px band behaves as recorded — indices 3, 4 and 5 land at 2944 / 2756 / 2686ms, uniformly late. At 390 only index 0 is on screen and there is no artifact.

### Option 3 ("cut at 4. Untested.") is now tested, and it is worse

Built with `priority={i < 4}` and measured the same way:

| width | n=3 | n=4 | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 390 | 832ms | 760ms | −72ms |
| 834 | 1536ms | 1292ms | −244ms |
| **1440** | 1872ms | **2888ms** | **+1016ms** |

It does what the issue predicted for the tablet row — the index 2 → index 3 gap closes from 1633ms to 758ms — and it pays for it with **a full second of LCP at 1440**.

That is the same mechanism this issue already documented for n=1: `priority` emits a preload and sets no `fetchpriority`, so a fourth preloaded card competes with the real LCP element on equal terms. At 1440 that fourth card is 63px visible, so the bandwidth goes to something almost off screen while the card that decides LCP waits.

Summed regret against the best value at each width: **n=3 costs 72+244 = 316ms, n=4 costs 1016ms.** n=3 remains the best available single number, now with the last untested alternative measured rather than assumed.

### Where that leaves it

Option 1 (accept) still holds, and its case is stronger than when it was written: the artifact is 1.6s rather than 2.7s, and every alternative is now measured rather than one of them being a guess.

Option 2 (a media-scoped preload) remains untried. Worth noting its stated ceiling of 84ms was about *LCP gain*, which is not what this artifact is — the artifact is a visual gap between two adjacent cards, and a preload scoped to `(min-width: 640px) and (max-width: 1023px)` would close it at 834 without the 1440 regression that sinks n=4. That is real hand-rolled machinery for one breakpoint band, which is why it has not been done, but the trade is different from the one the 84ms figure describes.

No code changed for this comment. `priority={i < 3}` is untouched.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

gh issue create --title "content-visibility defers the listing images with no JavaScript, which would close #261 outright" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Found while working #261. Filed rather than done, because it would replace the mechanism two merged pull requests just introduced.

## The measurement

Every card server-rendered as a plain `next/image` — no `DeferredImage`, no observer, no `<noscript>` — with `content-visibility: auto` and `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 400px` on the card box that already exists:

| viewport | no deferral | `DeferredImage` (shipped) | `content-visibility` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 390x844 | 7/21 | 6/21 | **4/21** |
| 834x1112 | 16/21 | 8/21 | **10/21** |
| 1440x900 | 21/21 | 12/21 | **12/21** |

So the browser does not fetch images inside a skipped subtree. The counts are comparable to the JavaScript deferral, and better at phone.

Everything else measured identical or better:

```
390x844:  docH 10690 -> 10690 after scrolling to bottom, CLS 0.0000, 21/21 card headings in DOM
834x1112: docH  6015 ->  6015                            CLS 0.0000, 21/21
1440x900: docH  3965 ->  3965                            CLS 0.0000, 21/21
```

Document heights are byte-for-byte what the shipped version produces. `content-visibility: auto` keeps content in the accessibility tree and findable by in-page search, unlike `display: none`.

## Why this matters more than the counts

**It closes #261.** That issue exists because a deferred image is not in the server-rendered HTML, so a blocked script leaves permanent empty boxes and `<noscript>` cannot help — it only fires when scripting is *off*, not when it loads and fails. With `content-visibility` every image is in the HTML. A failed chunk changes nothing at all.

It also removes, rather than mitigates:

- the pre-hydration hole that `eager={i < 6}` and `eager={i <= 1}` exist to close (#263 review), since nothing waits on hydration;
- the `<noscript>` fallback and its ~12x byte cost (5.1 MB against ~400 KB on the home page);
- `DeferredImage`, `ListingImage`'s composition of it, and their unit tests;
- the `rootMargin` tuning, which is currently a constant argued from pop-in measurements.

And it degrades in the safe direction: a browser without `content-visibility` fetches everything, which is exactly today's pre-#230 behaviour rather than a broken page.

## What has not been checked

Enough that this is a proposal, not a recommendation:

- **Browser support is recent.** Chrome 85, but Firefox 125 and Safari 18, both 2024. The degradation is graceful, but a meaningful share of visitors would get no deferral at all — which is worth knowing before deleting the mechanism that works everywhere.
- **`contain-intrinsic-size: auto 400px`** was picked to match the card box. `auto` remembers the real size once rendered; the 400px guess only applies before first render. Not tuned.
- **Scroll behaviour under fast flings** was not measured. Skipped subtrees have to render on approach, and that is layout work rather than a network fetch, so it fails differently from the pop-in the `rootMargin` was tuned against.
- **The home page** was not tested — only `/products/category/tents`. Its document is 5038px against this one's 3965px.
- **`priority` cards** sit above the fold and are never skipped, so the LCP preloads are unaffected, but that was reasoned rather than measured across viewports.

## Why it was not just done

It reverses the mechanism of #230 and #263, both merged today, and would delete a component, its tests and two `eager` cutoffs argued from measurements. That is a decision about how this app defers images, not a bug fix, and the browser-support tradeoff is a real one someone should make deliberately.

If it is taken, the honest sequence is: prove it on the home page too, decide whether Firefox 125 / Safari 18 baselines are acceptable, then delete rather than layer.

## Related

- #261 — closed outright by this, rather than mitigated.
- #230, #263 — the two changes whose mechanism this would replace.
- #262 — the square-source assumption, which `contain-intrinsic-size` would inherit.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

The one thing the old mechanism bought that CV does not is the 1200px `rootMargin` lead, and your fling column is the measurement that covers it (3/3, 6/6, 2 vs 3, 9 vs 7). Two PRs unwound on that evidence is fine.

**Is the conditional the right shape?** Yes, and it should stay a conditional rather than moving the empty state out of the box. The box carries `aspect-square w-full overflow-hidden rounded-3xl bg-gray-200`; the empty state's `flex h-full w-full items-center justify-center` depends on that box for its height. Hoisting it would duplicate the box or lose the centring. `product.image` is `string | null`, so the `&&` yields `null`/`""`/the class, all of which `clsx` handles, and it uses exactly the same truthiness as the ternary below it — the two cannot drift apart. `page.test.tsx:95` pins both directions, which is the right place for it since no seeded product lacks an image.

not when it loads and fails. There is nothing left to block.

So the deletions are the change, not a tidy-up: the observer, the
1200px margin argued from pop-in measurements, the placeholder that
swapped for an image, the `<noscript>` fallback costing 12x the
optimised bytes, both `eager` cutoffs, and the jsdom polyfill that
existed only to make the observer testable. Each was logic that needed
tests because it was logic. The browser was always willing to make this
decision itself.

`priority={i < 3}` on the category grid is untouched. It answers a
different question -- which card paints last -- and its cutoff is argued
from largest-contentful-paint medians.

The category box is skippable only when it holds an image. Both branches
of its ternary share that box and they are not alike: the image is
`alt=""` and contributes nothing to the accessibility tree, while the
empty state is text, and content in a skipped subtree is absent from the
accessibility tree until it renders -- measured against an on-screen
control. No seeded product lacks an image, so `page.test.tsx` pins both
directions where the journeys cannot reach.

No `contain-intrinsic-size`: `w-full` resolves against a definite grid
track and `aspect-square` gives the ratio, so the height is computed
from a definite width whether the subtree is skipped or not. Size
containment never has an intrinsic size to zero.

Closes #261
Refs #230, #263, #273
EOF
